answer: Zero-knowledge nullifier credentials resist Sybil attacks by having an accredited registrar blind-sign an operator's secret commitment, which the agent converts into a deterministic on-chain nullifier proof without exposing personal data. Because attackers cannot forge registrar keys or reuse a spent nullifier, hollow accounts flake away like shale, forcing one verified legal identity per agent. However, relying on centralized registrars risks censorship and excludes undocumented users.
